_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::fsi#20 and a FALSIFICATION. The entry claimed a fast inflow ramp 'produces Newton divergence within ~10 time steps even at laminar Re'. The upstream 2D FSI driven-cavity benchmark fsi_dc_mono_fs_ga_ga.4C.yaml already uses precisely the slow ramp the entry recommends (FUNCT1 = y*(1-cos(2*t*pi/5)), FUNCT2 = (1-cos(2*t*pi/5)), a 5 s cosine) over 10 steps of dt = 0.1. Replacing it with an instantaneous step to the same peak amplitude (y*2 and 2) holds the amplitude fixed and varies only the rate. Both arms complete all 10 time steps, neither prints a single non-convergence or divergence message, and the step arm takes 148 Newton steps against 81 -- 83% more work, not a failure. It exits nonzero only because the answer moved: 'Result check failed with 9 errors out of 9 tests', structure dispx at node 38 = -2.650e-03 against the pinned 2.467e-05. The real cost of a fast ramp on this benchmark is iterations and a different solution, not divergence. Both arms had the deck's relative MueLu xml path rewritten to an absolute one; that edit is identical in both. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C (2026.2.0-dev, git 89519cfe76).
expect_in_output: Result check failed with 9 errors out of 9 tests

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: give the step arm the same 5 s cosine ramp as the control. The two arms become identical, STEP_ARM_KEEPS_THE_COSINE_RAMP becomes 2 (forbidden), the Newton counts equalise so the verdict flips to 'no' (forbidden) and EXIT_STEP becomes 0 (forbidden), so the fixture must go red.
